title: Plasma/laser: common-line cutting in a nest, and marking before cutting

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: plasma/laser nesting cuts every part as its own closed profile with its own pierce and leads. Parts with a shared straight edge cannot be cut with one pass along that edge (common-line cutting), and there is no "mark before cut" ordering.

Wanted:
- Common-line cutting: in a nest, two parts placed one kerf width apart along a straight edge are cut with a single pass there. The paths of both parts are re-ordered so the shared edge is cut once and no part drops before its remaining edges are cut. A user option on the nest (off by default), with the kerf from the tool.
- Marking first: operations flagged as marking (low-power scribe or engrave) run before any cutting on the sheet.

Safety: a part must not be cut free while a later pass still has to run on it or start from it (a tipped part is a torch collision). The shared pass must leave both parts to size (kerf centred on the gap). Pierces stay off the part outline. Refuse by name when the gap is not one kerf wide or the shared edges are not parallel.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published material on common-line cutting and cut sequencing for sheet nests; the code is written from that and named in the provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: two rectangles nested with a shared edge post one pass on that edge and one pierce fewer; both parts measure to size in the path check; the cut-order test proves no part is free before its last pass; golden .nc for the plasma post; MCP option; the literature used is cited in the PR.
